extractor: read from the Ministry of Labour page registered in source_roles, fetched from the VPS with the source monitor's own User-Agent
policy: Every entry quotes the official page it was read from, verbatim and in Arabic. Labels and descriptions are VisaAI's English and are ours, not the authority's. This is a WORK PERMIT, not a visa: the Royal Oman Police decides entry and residence and serves its visa catalogue as client-rendered script, so nothing about the entry visa is recorded here.
structure_note:
THE FEE DEPENDS ON THE OCCUPATION CATEGORY, NOT THE WORKER. Ministerial Decision 340/2016 sets three bands — 301, 251 and 201 rial — and which band applies is decided by the occupation classification file the ministry publishes separately. An employer cannot price a hire from this page alone, and the page says so.

TWO VERIFICATIONS HAPPEN AUTOMATICALLY and remove documents from the file: the civil number is checked against the Civil Status Directorate, and the commercial register against the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, so registry documents need not be attached.
freshness_note: The pages carry an 'آخر تحديث' (last updated) stamp of 25/08/2026 in the site chrome rather than on the content itself, so it is recorded as a site-level stamp and not treated as a content dateline. The fee tables cite their own legal instruments — Ministerial Decision 340/2016 as amended, and 602/2025 as amended — which date the RULES even where they do not date the page.
not_extracted: The entry visa. A non-Omani worker needs both a Ministry of Labour work permit and a Royal Oman Police visa. evisa.rop.gov.om serves 44,892 bytes normalising to 927 characters because its catalogue is rendered by script, and www.rop.gov.om normalises to zero. Nobody has refused us; there is no text to read.

The 'دليل الخدمات' (services guide). Every page defers the per-activity and per-occupation document lists to this guide rather than stating them, and links it as a separate document. It is not fetched and its contents are not paraphrased.
The occupation classification file for private-sector establishments, which decides which fee category a job falls into. Linked, not stated.
Whether a fee figure is current. The pages cite ministerial decisions by number and year but publish no effective date for the amounts themselves.

requirements.description: A relief rather than a requirement, and it is the kind of thing an employer will otherwise prepare needlessly.

requirements.label: Processing and approval takes one to two weeks, depending on what the application requires
requirements.description: The page names the causes of delay: Omanisation analysis for establishments not meeting their quota, other conditions, document review, and activities requiring an inspection visit before authorisation.
requirements.source_excerpt: تتفاوت مدة معالجة و اعتماد الطلبات المقدمة من أسبوع الى أسبوعين بناء على الطلب وما يتطلبه من إجراءات مثل تحليل التعمين بالنسبة للمنشآت غيرالمحققة لنسبة التعمين ، و استيفاء الاشتراطات الأخرى و مراجعة الوثائق ، و الأنشطة التي تتطلب زيارة تفتيشية قبل التصريح لها .

requirements.label: The documents depend on the economic activity and the occupations being authorised, and are listed in the separate services guide
requirements.description: Three named categories: the municipal licence and lease contracts, documents by activity and occupation determined during the application, and approvals from competent bodies for specialised occupations in health, education and elsewhere.

requirements.description: Rial Omani. The category is decided by the ministry's separately published occupation classification file, so the fee cannot be determined from this page alone.
